Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: World Bank DTP (2023) explicitly states digital authentication capability is 'currently lacking' and 'existing legal ID systems require additional reforms to serve as a foundation for digital service delivery'. RNBP mobile app authentication not yet widely deployed.
revision_notes: World Bank Digital Transformation Project PID (2023) and Digital Economy Diagnostic (2023) both fetched and read; both explicitly state secure digital authentication capability 'is currently lacking' in Chad and that existing legal ID systems require reform before they can underpin digital service delivery, supporting the 'No' score. However, a Biometric Update article (16 Mar 2026, single source, not independently corroborated) reports that ANATS has signed an interoperability agreement with the Ministry of Finance enabling real-time identity verification/authentication via the national biometric registry, with plans to extend to other ministries and the private sector. This is a live, recent, but not yet independently verified change in status; per the single-source rule this is not sufficient on its own to upgrade the score. Flagged for human review to confirm whether the 2026 interoperability rollout constitutes a live digital authentication function.
revised_comments: Chad's national digital identity system does not yet provide a broadly operational digital authentication function. As of the World Bank's 2023 assessments, Chad lacked secure mechanisms for individuals to authenticate themselves or digitally verify documents, and its legal identification systems required further reform to serve as a foundation for digital service delivery. In March 2026, the National Agency for Secure Documents (ANATS) signed an interoperability agreement with the Ministry of Finance to enable real-time identity verification via the national biometric registry, with plans to expand this capability to other government bodies and the private sector, indicating this function is now emerging.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: Chad ranked 189th/193 countries on 2022 UN E-Government Development Index. No government-to-person (G2P) or government-to-business (G2B) transactional digital services in place. No government portal authentication using digital ID.
revision_notes: Both cited World Bank documents fetched and read. The 2023 Digital Economy Diagnostic and the 2023 Digital Transformation Project PID both confirm Chad ranked 189th of 193 countries on the 2022 UN E-Government Development Index and that no government-to-person (G2P) or government-to-business (G2B) transactional digital services, including centralised portal authentication, exist. No subsequent evidence of a centralised government authentication portal was found. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Chad has no centralised government portal or digital gateway through which citizens can authenticate using their digital ID. The country ranked 189th of 193 countries on the UN's 2022 E-Government Development Index, and government digital systems remain siloed back-office platforms (for example, for public finance and customs) rather than end-user-facing services; no government-to-person or government-to-business transactional portal exists.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Chad's KYC/AML regulations under CEMAC Regulation No. 01/03 require identity verification by financial institutions. ANATS-issued IDs accepted for KYC. RNBP enables identity verification via NNI. Refugees specifically noted as needing ANATS ID to open bank accounts.
revision_notes: Original Smile ID and Biometric Update sources reviewed. Additional 2026 sources (VoveID fintech onboarding guide, Didit identity verification page, Smile ID country page) fetched and confirm Chad's KYC/AML regime rests on CEMAC Regulation No. 01/03/CEMAC/UMAC/CM, supervised by BEAC, COBAC and the national financial intelligence unit (ANIF/ANLUFT), with national ID cards, passports and residence permits accepted as standard identity documents for onboarding. Commercial eKYC vendors (Smile ID, Didit, VoveID) actively verify Chadian ID documents for financial institutions, though sources note there is no centralised government API for real-time verification, so KYC relies on document capture and biometric face-matching rather than instant database checks. This still meets the threshold of 'enables KYC packet collection'. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Chad's identity system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) data collection for financial services. KYC/AML obligations are set at the CEMAC regional level under Regulation No. 01/03/CEMAC/UMAC/CM, enforced by BEAC, COBAC and Chad's financial intelligence unit. Financial institutions and fintechs verify customers using the ANATS-issued national ID card, passport or residence permit, typically supported by third-party document and biometric verification providers. There is no centralised government API for real-time verification, so KYC checks rely on document capture and biometric face-matching rather than instant database confirmation.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: SIGPTS integrated with civil registry at central level from early 2023. Health facility-based registration added since 2023 (120,000+ children registered). Birth registration rate remains low (~26%). Full integration not yet achieved.
revision_notes: All three original sources fetched and read. The World Bank PID confirms SIGPTS integrates civil registration and ID issuance at the central level via ANATS, with birth registration remaining low (26%, versus the 43% Sub-Saharan Africa average). The June 2025 Biometric Update article on the ID4Africa 2025 AGM corroborates that Chad's civil registry has been integrated with health facilities since 2023 (120,000+ children registered), schools (180,000+ pupils registered) and mobile/nomadic enrolment, but coverage gaps remain and full nationwide integration is not yet achieved. Score confirmed as partial integration.
revised_comments: Chad's civil registration and digital ID systems are partially integrated. The National Agency for Secure Documents (ANATS) has centralised civil registration and the biometric ID register (SIGPTS/RNBP) since early 2023, and has extended registration points into hospitals, schools and nomadic communities, registering over 120,000 children through health facilities and over 180,000 pupils through school campaigns since 2023. However, national birth registration remains low at around 26%, well below the Sub-Saharan African average, so full integration across the country has not yet been achieved.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Act No. 007/PR/2015 establishes data sharing rules requiring ANSICE authorization for transfers involving biometric/national ID data and cross-border transfers. Rules exist but World Bank notes enforcement gaps and regulatory capacity limitations.
revision_notes: DLA Piper and World Bank sources fetched and read. Act No. 007/PR/2015 (Personal Data Protection Act) and its 2019 implementing decree set out lawful processing, consent, and cross-border transfer requirements, with ANSICE empowered to authorise transborder data transfers. However, the World Bank's 2023 assessment notes ongoing regulatory capacity and enforcement gaps, and no ID-system-specific public data-sharing framework or published data-sharing agreements were found. Score of 'partially available' confirmed.
revised_comments: Procedural rules governing the collection, storage and sharing of personal data, including biometric identity data, are partially available in Chad. Act No. 007/PR/2015 on the Protection of Personal Data, together with its 2019 implementing decree, sets out lawful processing obligations, consent requirements and rules for cross-border data transfer, which require ANSICE authorisation. However, there is no dedicated, publicly documented data-sharing framework specific to the ID system, and enforcement and regulatory capacity remain limited.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No standalone digital ID-specific legislation identified. SIGPTS/ANATS governed by presidential decree, general data protection law (Act 007/PR/2015), and cybersecurity law. World Bank notes legal and regulatory gaps remain.
revision_notes: World Bank and DLA Piper sources fetched and read; no standalone digital ID-specific law was identified in either source or in supplementary searches. SIGPTS/ANATS operate under a 2016 presidential ordinance and Chad's general data protection, cybersecurity and electronic transactions laws (Acts 006-009/PR/2015), rather than a dedicated digital ID statute. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Chad has no standalone legislation specific to digital identity. The national ID system (SIGPTS, managed by ANATS) operates under a 2016 presidential ordinance establishing ANATS and under Chad's general legal framework for data protection (Act 007/PR/2015), electronic transactions (Act 008/PR/2015) and cybersecurity (Act 009/PR/2015), rather than a dedicated digital ID law.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Act No. 007/PR/2015 on Personal Data Protection enacted February 10, 2015. Implementing Decree No. 075/PR/2019. Establishes lawful processing requirements, data subject rights, and sanctions.
revision_notes: DLA Piper page and a 2026 data-protection law summary (Anurag Verma Worldwatch) both fetched and read, confirming Act No. 007/PR/2015 on the Protection of Personal Data (10 February 2015), implemented by Decree No. 075/PR/2019, remains in force and covers personal data generally, including data processed by the ID system. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Chad has enacted comprehensive data protection legislation. Act No. 007/PR/2015 on the Protection of Personal Data, signed 10 February 2015 and implemented by Decree No. 075/PR/2019, governs the collection, processing, storage and transmission of personal data, including biometric and identity data processed under the national ID system.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: ANSICE (Agence Nationale de Sécurité Informatique et de Certification Électronique) is Chad's data protection authority, established by Act No. 006/PR/2015. Has investigative, advisory, and sanctioning powers over data processing including ID systems.
revision_notes: DLA Piper's dedicated 'Authority' page and the 2026 Worldwatch summary both fetched and read, confirming ANSICE (Agence Nationale de Sécurité Informatique et de Certification Électronique), created under Act No. 006/PR/2015, is Chad's designated data protection authority, with powers to investigate, sanction, and authorise cross-border data transfers. Sources confirm ANSICE became fully operational in 2020. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: A dedicated Data Protection Authority oversees personal data processing in Chad, including data held by the ID system. The Agence Nationale de Sécurité Informatique et de Certification Électronique (ANSICE), created under Act No. 006/PR/2015, became fully operational in 2020 and has powers to investigate complaints, authorise cross-border data transfers, and sanction violations of the data protection law.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: National ID card issued by ANATS serves as legal proof of identity for government services, voting, banking, and travel. NNI embedded in credentials is the authoritative unique identifier.
revision_notes: World Bank PID fetched and read; it confirms the ANATS-issued national ID card (via the NNI/SIGPTS system) is the recognised basis for accessing government services, banking and other transactions. The Wikipedia list of national ID card policies is a weak, non-authoritative source offering no substantive confirmation beyond noting that Chad issues a national ID card; it is not relied upon. Score confirmed on the strength of the World Bank source.
revised_comments: The ANATS-issued national ID card, underpinned by the biometric National Identification Number (NNI), serves as the recognised basis for proving identity in Chad, accepted for government services, banking (KYC) and other transactions.

Comments: ANATS established by presidential decree in 2016. Broader legal framework includes Act No. 007/PR/2015 (Data Protection), Act No. 006/PR/2015 (ANSICE), Ordonnance No 002/PR/2020 on civil status organisation.
revision_notes: World Bank PID and DLA Piper sources fetched and read; both confirm ANATS was established by presidential ordinance in 2016, operating alongside Act No. 007/PR/2015 (data protection), Act No. 006/PR/2015 (ANSICE) and a 2020 ordinance reorganising civil status. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Formal legislation underpins Chad's identity system. ANATS, the agency responsible for the national ID and civil registration system, was established by presidential ordinance in 2016, and operates within a wider legal framework comprising the 2015 Personal Data Protection Act, the 2015 Act creating ANSICE, and a 2020 ordinance reorganising civil status administration.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: SIGPTS technology provided by IDEMIA (French multinational). ANATS holds a 3-year maintenance contract with IDEMIA costing ~2.9 billion XAF (~US$4.8M). Foreign vendor dominates system maintenance.
revision_notes: World Bank diagnostic and two Biometric Update articles (May 2025, March 2026) fetched and read; all confirm the French firm IDEMIA continues to supply and maintain the underlying SIGPTS/biometric registry technology, including its most recent refugee ID and interoperability rollouts. No evidence found of maintenance shifting to in-country technical staff. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: System maintenance for Chad's biometric ID platform (SIGPTS) remains dominated by the foreign vendor IDEMIA, which built and continues to support the underlying technology, including the biometric deduplication engine and recent refugee registration and interoperability rollouts. ANATS held a multi-year maintenance contract with IDEMIA valued at approximately XAF 2.9 billion (around US$4.8 million); no evidence indicates a shift toward in-country technical management.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: SIGPTS/ANATS primarily dependent on external financing. World Bank's Chad Digital Transformation Project (P180000, 2023) funds digital ID improvements. Some user fees collected (10,000 CFA per ID card) but far insufficient for system costs of ~2.9B XAF for IDEMIA contract alone.
revision_notes: World Bank PID (2023) and the September 2024 Chad Digital Transformation Project Appraisal Document (US$92.2m IDA grant) both fetched and read, confirming continued heavy reliance on external World Bank financing for ID system development. A March 2026 Biometric Update article reports approximately XAF 15 billion (~US$26.1m) of domestic investment in the biometric registry 'over the last few years', which is meaningful but small relative to the US$92.2m 2024 World Bank grant and US$120m Safety Nets grant that also fund ID-linked systems. External funding remains dominant. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Ongoing development of Chad's ID system remains primarily dependent on external donor financing. The World Bank has approved a US$92.2 million grant (2024) for the Chad Digital Transformation Project, which funds ID and civil registration modernisation, alongside other donor-funded programmes such as the US$120 million Adaptive and Productive Safety Nets Project. Domestic investment, reported at approximately XAF 15 billion (around US$26.1 million) over recent years, is comparatively modest against this external financing.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: SIGPTS collects fingerprints (stored on national ID card chip for 1:1 matching) and palm prints for verification. No confirmed facial/iris biometrics in SIGPTS.
revision_notes: World Bank diagnostic and Biometric Update sources fetched and read; both confirm SIGPTS collects fingerprints (and palm prints) for biometric matching. No source found confirming facial image or iris capture as part of routine SIGPTS enrolment, distinct from UNHCR's separate BIMS system (which does capture iris and facial images for refugees generally, but is not documented as part of the ANATS/SIGPTS enrolment process). Score confirmed, though evidence on facial capture is not fully conclusive.
revised_comments: Chad's biometric ID system (SIGPTS/RNBP) collects fingerprint biometrics as its core modality for identity deduplication and verification, alongside a printed photograph on the credential. No confirmed evidence of routine facial-recognition or iris biometric capture as part of standard SIGPTS enrolment was found.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: RNBP (Registre National Biométrique des Populations) is a centralized digital biometric database. SIGPTS launched 2020. Civil registration historically paper-based but digitalization underway under ANATS.
revision_notes: World Bank diagnostic and PID both fetched and read; confirm the National Biometric Register of Populations (RNBP) is a centralised digital biometric database managed by ANATS since 2020, while separate general civil registration remains largely paper-based outside health facility and school digitisation points. As the RNBP/SIGPTS system covered by this variable is fully digital, score confirmed.
revised_comments: Identity records within Chad's national biometric ID system are stored digitally. The National Biometric Register of Populations (RNBP), operated by ANATS through the SIGPTS platform since 2020, is a centralised electronic database, distinct from the largely paper-based general civil registration system that is being progressively digitised through integration with health facilities and schools.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: SIGPTS (Integrated Population and Secure Documents Management System) launched in 2020 by ANATS, deploying biometric NNI and national ID. Operational in capital and some regions; national rollout ongoing. Coverage remains very low (~3-6% of eligible population).
revision_notes: All original and newly fetched sources confirm SIGPTS/RNBP, launched in 2020 and managed by ANATS, is operational and expanding (refugee registration pilot from 2025, Ministry of Finance interoperability agreement March 2026), but population coverage remains very low (3-8% depending on measure and year, see population coverage variable). The system is deployed but nowhere near nationwide saturation, consistent with 'partially deployed' rather than 'fully deployed nationwide'. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: Chad has established and is actively expanding a national digital identity system. The Integrated Population and Secure Documents Management System (SIGPTS), managed by the National Agency for Secure Documents (ANATS) and launched in 2020 using IDEMIA biometric technology, issues a biometric National Identification Number (NNI) and national ID card. It is operational in the capital and a growing number of provinces, and has recently been extended to refugee populations and linked to the Ministry of Finance for real-time verification, but overall population coverage remains low, so the system is best characterised as partially deployed rather than fully rolled out nationwide.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: SIGPTS is interoperable with civil registration at central level since early 2023. Integration with health/education/land sectors potential but not yet operationalized. Digital authentication capability still lacking for broad cross-sector use.
revision_notes: World Bank sources (2023) confirm SIGPTS was integrated with civil registration at the central level from early 2023. This is now reinforced by a March 2026 Biometric Update article confirming ANATS signed an interoperability agreement with the Ministry of Finance for real-time data sharing based on the national biometric registry, with plans for wider ministry and private-sector integration, described by ANATS as intended to make the registry 'the single source of truth for all identification purposes'. Score of 'Yes' confirmed and strengthened by more recent evidence.
revised_comments: Chad's digital ID system is interoperable with other government systems. The biometric registry underlying SIGPTS has been integrated with civil registration since early 2023, and in March 2026 the National Agency for Secure Documents (ANATS) signed an interoperability agreement with the Ministry of Finance enabling real-time data sharing and identity verification, with plans to extend integration to further government agencies and private-sector entities.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: National ID card accepted by financial institutions for KYC/AML under CEMAC regulations. Not universally mandatory; alternative documents sometimes accepted. Refugees specifically lost bank access without ANATS-issued IDs.
revision_notes: Original Smile ID and Biometric Update sources plus a 2026 fintech KYC guide fetched and read; all confirm the ANATS national ID card is one of several accepted identity documents (alongside passport and residence permit) for bank account opening under CEMAC KYC/AML rules, but is not the sole mandatory credential. Refugees without an ANATS ID have been reported unable to open bank accounts, reflecting de facto reliance on the credential in some cases, but it is not universally mandatory. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: The national ID card is accepted, but not mandatory, for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services in Chad. Financial institutions verify customers under CEMAC KYC/AML rules using any of several accepted documents, including the ANATS-issued national ID card, passport or residence permit. In practice, refugees without an ANATS-issued identity document have faced difficulty accessing banking services, illustrating the credential's practical importance even though it is not the sole legal requirement.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: National ID card issued to persons over 12 years old (World Bank DTP 2023). Refugee IDs issued to ages 10+ per Chadian law. NNI assigned from birth registration. Physical biometric ID enrollment begins at approximately age 10-12.
revision_notes: World Bank PID and Biometric Update refugee ID article both fetched and read; confirm national ID card enrolment begins at approximately age 12 (World Bank, 2023) and refugee ID (NNIR) enrolment from age 10, consistent with Chadian law providing for identification from age 10 upward. Score of '10-17' confirmed.
revised_comments: Individuals become eligible to enrol for Chad's biometric national ID card at around 12 years of age, per World Bank reporting on the SIGPTS system; the parallel refugee identification programme enrols from age 10, consistent with Chadian law. Birth registration and NNI assignment occur separately from birth, but physical biometric ID enrolment does not begin until later childhood.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: Refugees without ANATS digital ID noted as unable to receive healthcare. National ID accepted at health facilities. Health facilities integrated into civil registration system since 2023. Not formally mandatory for all healthcare access.
revision_notes: Both Biometric Update articles fetched and read; confirm refugees without an ANATS ID have faced barriers accessing healthcare, and that civil registration has been integrated with health facilities since 2023 (over 120,000 children registered through hospital-based registry offices), but no evidence of a formal mandatory ID requirement for general healthcare access was found. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: The national ID credential is accepted, but not formally mandatory, for accessing public healthcare in Chad. Since 2023 the civil registration and ID system has been integrated with health facilities, with over 120,000 children registered through hospital-based registry offices, and refugees without an ANATS-issued identity document have reported difficulty accessing healthcare services, reflecting the credential's practical, though not strictly compulsory, role.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: World Bank Digital Transformation Project (2023) reports only 3% of the Chadian population (over 12 years old) holds a National ID card. World Bank Diagnostic notes 5-6% in SIGPTS database. Well below 20%.
revision_notes: World Bank Digital Transformation Project PID (2023, 3% of population over 12 hold a national ID card), the Digital Economy Diagnostic (2023, 5-6%), and the September 2024 Chad Digital Transformation Project Appraisal Document (2024, only 8% of the population issued the NNI/biometric ID, versus 39% holding some form of legacy/paper national ID) were all fetched and read. All figures for the biometric/digital ID system specifically are well below the 20% threshold, even as the broader 'national ID' figure (including older non-biometric documents) is somewhat higher. Score of '<20%' confirmed using the digital/biometric ID coverage figures most relevant to this variable.
revised_comments: Population coverage of Chad's biometric digital ID system remains very low. As of 2024, only around 8% of the population had been issued the biometric National Identification Number (NNI) under the SIGPTS/RNBP system, up from approximately 3% (2023) and 5-6% (2023) of the population aged over 12 holding a national ID card in earlier assessments. A broader, though less directly comparable, figure of 39% is cited for general national ID ownership inclusive of older, non-biometric documents.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: National ID card and birth certificate accepted for access to social services including education. Having an ANATS NNI improves access to basic services for refugees. Not universally mandatory for all social services.
revision_notes: World Bank PID and Biometric Update refugee ID article both fetched and read; confirm the national ID card and birth certificate are accepted for accessing social services and that the refugee National Identification Number (NNIR) improves access to basic services, without evidence of a universal mandatory requirement. Score confirmed.
revised_comments: The national ID card and birth certificate are accepted, but not universally mandatory, for registering for social assistance programmes and accessing social services in Chad. Holding the ANATS-issued National Identification Number (NNI), including the parallel refugee NNIR, is reported to improve access to basic services and protect service providers against fraud, though it is not a strict precondition for all social service access.
